abstract: Providing inclusive environments has become a primary tenet of modern societies and organizations. The use of gender-inclusive language (GIL) is often considered an instrument that can promote inclusion, yet little is known about its effects on relevant economic behaviors and on gender gaps in the labor market. GIL avoids the masculine “default” (common to many languages) by either explicitly mentioning both masculine and feminine (pro)nouns, or replacing them with nongendered (pro)nouns. Here we study the causal short-run impact of GIL on competitiveness and leadership in the laboratory, with two different language samples—English and German—which differ, among other things, in the extent to which gender is embedded linguistically. We vary GIL in experimental instructions across three treatments ([Formula: see text]): a masculine baseline condition, a condition with feminine and masculine (pro)nouns, and a condition with nongendered (pro)nouns. We find that participants who identify as female and participants who identify as male compete, stand for leadership, and vote on leader candidates similarly across all treatments, in either language. Furthermore, we find no treatment differences in participants’ feelings of inclusion and perceived entitlement. In sum, there is a lack of support for GIL having short-term causal effects on competitive and leadership behavior and inclusion perceptions. This paper was accepted by Marie-Claire Villeval, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: This work was supported by the Austrian Science Fund [Grant SFB F63], UK Research and Innovation [Grant MR/T020253/1], the University of Exeter, and Regensburger Universitätsstiftung Lucia and Dr. Otfried Eberz. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04342 .
abstract_zh: 提供包容性环境已成为现代社会和组织的一项首要原则。使用性别包容性语言（GIL）常被视为一种能够促进包容的工具，但人们对其对相关经济行为以及劳动力市场中性别差距的影响知之甚少。GIL通过明确提及男性和女性（代）名词，或用无性别（代）名词替代它们，避免了男性“默认”（许多语言中常见）。在此，我们在实验室中研究GIL对竞争力和领导力的因果短期影响，采用两个不同的语言样本——英语和德语——它们在诸多方面有所不同，其中包括性别在语言中嵌入的程度。我们在实验指令中变化GIL，分为三种处理（[公式：见正文]）：男性基线条件、包含女性和男性（代）名词的条件，以及包含无性别（代）名词的条件。我们发现，自我认同为女性和自我认同为男性的参与者，在两种语言的所有处理中，其竞争、竞选领导职位以及对领导候选人投票的行为都相似。此外，我们发现参与者的包容感和感知权利在处理之间没有差异。总之，缺乏支持GIL对竞争和领导行为以及包容感知具有短期因果效应的证据。本文由Marie-Claire Villeval，行为经济学与决策分析领域接受。资助：本工作得到奥地利科学基金[资助号SFB F63]、英国研究与创新[资助号MR/T020253/1]、埃克塞特大学以及雷根斯堡大学基金会Lucia and Dr. Otfried Eberz的支持。补充材料：在线附录和数据文件可在https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04342获取。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Gender-Inclusive Language and Economic Decision-Making
title_zh: 性别包容性语言与经济决策

abstract: This work explores the preferences that laypeople exhibit when making and evaluating predictions in the form of point estimates (e.g., the high temperature will be 66°). I propose that people typically have diminishing sensitivity to prediction error: the absolute difference between a prediction and a realized outcome. As a result, people often prioritize “being right,“ focusing on achieving near perfect predictions and placing less emphasis on the magnitude of errors when errors occur. Across 16 studies using varying methods and stimuli, participants exhibited multiple behaviors consistent with diminishing sensitivity to prediction error: (i) predicting the mode of distributions, (ii) restricting predictions to possible outcomes, (iii) reporting decreasing reactions to increasing marginal units of error, and (iv) preferring predictive models built with diminishing sensitivity to error. This behavior diverges from traditional methods of building predictive models and common interpretations of people’s predictions, which often prioritize avoiding large errors and assume that people are predicting the mean. Ultimately, this work not only highlights the discrepancies between our current practices and people’s preferences for predictions but also calls for a more thorough exploration of human objectives before we build models for them to use or make inferences about their beliefs in light of a decision they made. This paper was accepted by Jack Soll, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: I thank the University of Chicago Booth School of Business for financial support. Supplemental Material: Preregistrations, materials, data, code, and supplements are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07257 and at ResearchBox at https://researchbox.org/3130 .
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了普通人在以点估计形式（例如，最高气温将为66°）进行预测和评估预测时所表现出的偏好。我提出，人们通常对预测误差——即预测值与实际结果之间的绝对差——具有递减敏感性。因此，人们往往优先考虑“预测准确”，专注于实现接近完美的预测，而在出现误差时较少强调误差的幅度。在16项采用不同方法和刺激材料的研究中，参与者表现出多种与对预测误差的递减敏感性相一致的行为：(i) 预测分布的众数，(ii) 将预测限制在可能结果范围内，(iii) 报告对递增的边际误差单位反应递减，以及 (iv) 偏好以对误差的递减敏感性构建的预测模型。这种行为偏离了构建预测模型的传统方法以及对人们预测的常见解读，后者往往优先考虑避免大误差，并假设人们在预测均值。最终，本研究不仅凸显了我们当前实践与人们对预测的偏好之间的差异，也呼吁在构建供人们使用的模型、或根据人们所做决策推断其信念之前，对人类目标进行更彻底的探索。本文由Jack Soll、行为经济学与决策分析领域接收。资助：我感谢芝加哥大学布斯商学院提供的财务支持。补充材料：预注册、材料、数据、代码和补充内容可在 https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07257 以及 ResearchBox 的 https://researchbox.org/3130 获取。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Understanding People’s Preferences for Predictions: People Prioritize Being Right over Minimizing How Wrong They Are in Expectation
title_zh: 理解人们对预测的偏好：人们更重视正确性而非最小化预期错误程度
